resolved_conflicts.explanation: The survey says steel towers replaced the wood tower in the 1940s or 1950s; Landforms marks the site removed with no date. Both can hold. The story reports both and does not say where the steel tower stood or when it came down, because neither source says.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: a Landforms table row (name, county, 857 ft, state no. 7-10, removed), one NRHP survey passage (wood-built; replaced by steel in the 1940s or 1950s, citing an undated TDF record), and the survey's 2014 extant list, which names three Hickman County towers (Hornertown, Moores Switch, Weatherly) but not Cobel. Absence from that list is not proof of removal and is not stated as one. The brief's coordinates (35.7240, -87.6733) and elevation (261.2 m) match Landforms' towers.gpx waypoint (cached at https://tnlandforms.us/towers/towers.gpx); not cited as a source because its coordinates are XML attributes the quote checker cannot read. No build date, builder, height, staffing, fire, or current site description found. The brief's record is correct on status and location; no corrections. A search surfaced an anyplaceamerica listing for a 'Coble Lookout Tower' in Hickman County (id 1319062); the page returned HTTP 403 and was not read; nothing here ties it to Cobel, so it is not used. NHLR and FFLOS caches have no Cobel entry. No photos found. Search budget: two websearch.py calls, both returning the same few leads.
